_about: The recipe scripts/ai-catalog.js turns into data/ai/catalog.ron (docs/design/embeddable-ai.md, 6.2; rung 2, 2026-11-09). Edit THIS file, never the catalog: the script measures each file (its size and SHA-256), refuses one that does not match its publisher's hash, splits anything of 2 GiB or more into parts, and writes the catalog the app compiles in. Only what can be downloaded today is listed: Ministral 3 3B, Gemma 4 and Pocket TTS are absent until their rungs bring their files (data/ai/choices.ron still shows what each will need).
_part_bytes: GitHub's limit is 'Each file included in a release must be under 2 GiB' (the runtime finding, F10): a file of 2 GiB or more goes up as parts of this size, each with its own hash, joined and checked whole after download.

engine._credits: Rows in data/credits.ron (scripts/check-ai-catalog.js refuses a catalog entry without one): llama.cpp and ggml, whose code is inside the engine; and the llama-cpp-rs project, whose crate llama-cpp-sys-2 carries the pinned llama.cpp source the engine builds (none of its own code is compiled in).

extras._why: Apache 2.0 section 4(a): 'You must give any other recipients of the Work or Derivative Works a copy of this License'. The text is apache.org's (SHA-256 cfc7749b...), which the Granite finding (F1) compared with IBM's LICENSE line by line: the same, IBM's having one leading blank line.

extras.text: Granite 4.0 1B (Q4_K_M GGUF) by IBM, https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-4.0-1b-GGUF, Apache License 2.0. Unmodified. Training data disclosure: https://github.com/ibm-granite/granite-4.0-nano-language-models/tree/main/disclosures.
extras._why: The credit README exactly as the Granite finding wrote it ('How the project would credit it').
